result.notes:
Environment: mix/elixir reachable via asdf shims (`export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"`), not on default PATH -- Elixir 1.20.3-otp-29 / Erlang/OTP 29.

Baseline: `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs test/letflow/engine/lua_number_marshalling_test.exs` -> `Result: 64 passed` before any change.

MUTATION TESTING (both mutations named in the task brief, plus follow-ups):

1. get_instance_state self-instance check, equality swapped for `if true do`: do_get_instance_state/3's `if instance_id == execution_context.instance_id do ... else encode_error(lua, "forbidden") end` changed to `if true do ... end`. Result: 55/56 passed in platform_test.exs -- caught by "a real same-tenant sibling instance AND a nonexistent instance id both return the IDENTICAL forbidden result". Reverted; 56 passed again (diff against saved original confirmed byte-identical).

2. Same check, REORDERED to run AFTER the Repo call instead of before it: changed to call fetch_instance_state/3 unconditionally first, then apply the equality check only to choose which VALUE to return. Result: 56/56 passed UNCHANGED -- a real gap: no existing test verified the "no Repo call attempted at all" half of the design's own claim (design SS5.1 / moduledoc), only the return value. GAP CLOSED: added test "no Repo.get/3 (no [:letflow, :repo, :query] telemetry event) fires for a same-tenant sibling id" to platform_test.exs, using the same `:telemetry.attach/4` counter idiom test/letflow/api/context_test.exs already uses for the same purpose (own fixtures: a fresh provisioned_tenant/0, own_id/sibling_id both seeded, asserts the telemetry counter stays 0 across a forbidden call). Re-ran the SAME reordering mutation against the new suite: 56/57 passed, the new test the sole failure. Reverted; 57 passed. Diff against saved original platform.ex confirmed byte-identical after revert.

3. LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1, round float to 1 decimal (Float.round(value,1)): 65/65 passed UNCHANGED. Investigated: not a real gap -- both float fixture values in the suite (3.0, 2.5) are already exact at 1 decimal, so this specific mutation is coincidentally invisible for these inputs without being a real identity violation for them. Followed up with two mutations that ARE genuine identity violations, both caught (below), rather than concluding a gap from a coincidentally-unobservable mutation.

4. LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1, coerce whole-number float to integer (`value == trunc(value) -> trunc(value)`): 63/65 passed -- caught by the unit test's is_float/1 assertion AND the platform read_variable/get_instance_state round-trip test (2 failures). Reverted; 65 passed.

5. LuaNumberMarshalling.from_lua/1, coerce integer to string: 64/65 passed -- caught by the unit test "returns an integer unchanged". Reverted; 65 passed.

Every mutation was reverted and the byte-identical original confirmed via `diff` before moving to the next, per instructions -- only mutation 2 required adding a test; mutations 1, 4, 5 were already covered.

Design-doc addendum: added two 'Post-implementation cross-reference note' additions to lib/letflow/design/req159-lua-host-api-read.md (end of SS7.4 and end of SS6.4), matching the exact precedent style of req149-lua-memory-limit.md's addendum -- one documents run_stub/3 becoming run_stub/5 (not the design's literal run_stub/4) and why (arity-2 Lua.set!/3 callback form required to reach the call's own Lua.t() for Lua.encode!/2), the other documents log's explicit Lua.decode!/2 step on the context argument and why the design's 'already converted... by tv-labs/lua's own argument-marshalling' claim in SS6.1 step 1 is factually wrong per the vendored deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/value.ex source. Neither addendum changes any prior recommendation; both are documentation-only, non-blocking, and explicitly labeled as added by TEST-DESIGNER's Step 3 at REVIEWER's recommendation.

test/specs/REQ-159.md reconciled: replaced the pre-implementation skeleton's forward-looking language with a Status note explaining it predates implementation/rework, updated every relevant sub-bullet to cite the actual test name it maps to (including the new telemetry test), added a full AC-to-test mapping table using REQ-159's 8 acceptance_criteria VERBATIM from docs/requirements.yaml (not paraphrased), added a Test isolation section describing the real-Postgres provisioned_tenant/0 + seed_projection!/3 fixture idiom (per-test tenant id, on_exit drop-schema + row cleanup, async:false module-level requirement already forced by the pre-existing REQ-152 tests), a No wall-clock/unseeded-randomness section, and a Mutation testing section documenting all 5 mutations above with counts. AC-to-test mapping (REQ-159's 8 acceptance_criteria, verbatim from docs/requirements.yaml):
1. read_variable current-value-or-nil (LUA-11 read-half) -> 'returns the current value for a set variable', 'returns nil for an unset variable'
2. log emits structured entry w/ script identity+instance ID+trace ID, each asserted individually -> 'emits an entry with all three correlation fields, asserted individually, plus the message text' (3 separate assert log =~ lines)
3. get_instance_state returns state for valid instance / structured error (not a raise) for invalid -> 'returns state for the script's own valid instance'; the 4 structured-error tests (invalid_id/no_execution_context/not_found/forbidden), none using assert_raise
4. capability-denial test per function (read_variable/get_instance_state/log) each raising a Lua error -> the 3 'capability denial'/'raises a capability denial for ...' tests
5. number conversion uses REQ-150's named module/function; moduledoc cites REQ-150's section by number -> lua_number_marshalling_test.exs exercises LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1 and from_lua/1 directly; platform.ex moduledoc/inline docs cite LuaNumberMarshalling and REQ-150 (verified by direct reading)
6. round-trip integer AND float through read_variable, subtype matches REQ-150's rule -> 'round-trips an integer AND a float, proving LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1 is genuinely applied (AC6)'; also exercised via get_instance_state's 'returns state for the script's own valid instance' (both an integer and a float leaf)
7. no Repo call with a script-supplied prefix; moduledoc states prefix is supplied by calling engine code -> 'platform.ex's only Repo call site passes prefix: execution_context's own prefix, never a script-supplied value' (source-level structural guard) + the NEW telemetry test proving no Repo call at all fires on a forbidden path
8. mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted -> quoted above; TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 remains the authoritative run
